activity.notes: Lachlan Macquarie (1762–1824) assumed office as British Governor of the Colony of New South Wales on 1 January 1810 after the 1808 Rum Rebellion and handed the governorship to Thomas Brisbane on 1 December 1821. He oversaw a program of roads, civic buildings, social administration and changes to the treatment and integration of former convicts within settler society. His colonial record also includes military punitive expeditions that he directed against Aboriginal peoples: state primary archival material identifies his orders, and the Appin massacre occurred on 17 April 1816. These settler-state developments and harms to Indigenous communities must both be retained in historical interpretation; this Activity is the governor's actual office, not an independent 'Macquarie' polity.
